name: mcfadden cucumber salad
instructions:
Joshua McFadden's 'Cucumbers, Scallions, Mint, and Dried Chiles' (Six Seasons) — his go-to cucumber dish: cool cukes, hot chiles, fragrant mint, the whole greater than the sum of its parts. MY VERSION IS REFACTORED: the main ingredients are CUCUMBER + PEAR + SCALLION + CHAMPAGNE VINEGAR. Pears are a win; scallion is just the white part of one stalk, finely chopped — not too much. His red onion and mint are demoted to optional (see the too-many-ingredients note), and champagne vinegar is a huge win over the standard/sweet white wine vinegar he calls for.

SERVES 4.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 1 lb cucumbers (preferably a mix of colors and shapes)
- kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
- 1 bunch scallions, trimmed (including 1/2 inch off the green tops), sliced on a sharp angle, SOAKED IN ICE WATER 20 minutes, drained well
- 1/4 red onion, very thinly sliced
- 1 small handful mint leaves (a mix of varieties is great)
- 1/2 tsp dried chile flakes
- 3 tbsp CHAMPAGNE VINEGAR (my swap — McFadden calls for slightly sweet white wine vinegar, e.g. KATZ Sauvignon Blanc; see notes)
- extra-virgin olive oil (~1/4 cup)
- coarse finishing salt (Maldon or Jacobsen), optional

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. PREP THE CUCUMBERS: peel if skins are tough or waxed (for a typical green slicing cuke, peel in alternating stripes). Trim ends, halve lengthwise, scoop out the seeds. Slice into A VARIETY OF SHAPES: moons, angled slices, batons, small chunks.
2. SALT + DRAIN 30 MIN: toss the cucumbers with 1 tsp salt and put in a colander to draw out excess moisture. Sit 30 minutes, then BLOT on paper towels to remove moisture and excess salt. Pile into a large bowl.
3. COMBINE: add the scallions, onion, mint, chile flakes, vinegar, and a few generous grinds of black pepper. HOLD OFF ON THE SALT. Toss to blend. Taste and adjust — more chile flakes, black pepper, or salt if needed.
4. THE OIL: when the flavor is exciting and balanced, add 1/4 cup olive oil and toss. Taste and add more oil if needed to balance. You want PLENTY OF 'DRESSING' POOLING in the bottom of the bowl — the cucumbers keep drinking it up, and the juices should run into the other elements on the plate (grilled pork, etc).
5. Serve with a sprinkle of finishing salt, if you like, for crunch.
notes:
=== SOURCE ===

Joshua McFadden, Six Seasons ('Cucumbers, Scallions, Mint, and Dried Chiles' — Season Three: Midsummer). His framing: the key is the vinegar — he uses KATZ's slightly-sweet late-harvest Sauvignon Blanc vinegar.

=== CHAMPAGNE VINEGAR — THE HUGE WIN; SWEET WHITE WINE VINEGAR CLASHING ===

Got champagne vinegar to try with this and it's a HUGE WIN over standard/sweet white wine vinegar — which I think is CLASHING here. McFadden's whole point is that the vinegar is the key; he's right about the slot, and champagne vinegar is the better occupant (delicate where white wine vinegar is sharp, dry where his KATZ pick is sweet).

THE BIGGER PATTERN: sherry + champagne vinegar seem to UNBLOCK A LOT OF SIDES — sherry for the warm/earthy ones ([[sherry-french-lentils]]), champagne for the delicate/raw ones (here, and queued in [[lentil-cream-salad]] / [[cream-vinaigrette]]). More recipes on both expected.

=== HE ADDS TOO MANY INGREDIENTS — REFACTORED TO THE CORE ===

McFadden tends to add too many ingredients, and this recipe is no different. The refactored core: CUCUMBER + PEAR + SCALLION + CHAMPAGNE VINEGAR (+ chile flakes, oil, salt, pepper). Red onion and mint are secondary — fine, not structural.

=== PEARS — A WIN; CHAMPAGNE VINEGAR BEATS WHITE BALSAMIC WITH THEM ===

Pears are a WIN. Tested WHITE BALSAMIC with the pear (the rounder-sweeter theory) — and no: pears pair BETTER with CHAMPAGNE VINEGAR. The delicate-dry axis wins over the round-sweet one even for sweet fruit.

=== SCALLION — WHITE PART ONLY, ONE STALK, FINE ===

Green onions are a win too — but JUST THE WHITE PART of one stalk, finely chopped. Not too much.

=== OBSERVATIONS — SALT AND OIL ===

- SALT makes it taste more 'EAST ASIAN' somehow — the salted-cucumber + vinegar + chili combination drifts toward that register as the salt goes up. Worth knowing when calibrating.
- The OLIVE OIL seems to be there FOR THE CHILI FLAKE FLAVOR — it's the carrier that blooms and distributes the chile, more than a dressing fat in its own right.

=== BELL PEPPER — CLASHING ===

Bell pepper doesn't like the same vinegar families (the champagne/delicate axis this salad runs on). Keep it out.

=== HIS TECHNIQUE NOTES (ALL KEEPERS) ===

- SALT THE CUCUMBERS AHEAD (30 min in a colander, then blot): reduces sogginess by pulling moisture and gives a tighter, 'PICKLED' texture.
- ICE-WATER SOAK THE SCALLIONS (20 min): crisps them and tames the raw bite.
- VARIETY OF SHAPES on the cucumber cuts — moons, angles, batons, chunks.
- SALT LAST: the cucumbers come in pre-salted from the drain; hold off until after tasting.
- GENEROUS DRESSING POOL: the cucumbers keep drinking it, and the juices are meant to run into the rest of the plate (grilled pork is his example pairing).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[kachumber]]: the indian cucumber salad (lime + mango axis) — this is the mediterranean/midsummer counterpart.
- [[cucumber-avocado-smoothie]]: the blended cucumber direction.
- [[relish]]: the other food-processor-era crunchy condiment; this salad keeps everything whole instead.

=== BASIL — TRIED, UNDECIDED ===

Tried basil (the too-many-salads-have-mint motivation). The LEAVES ARE A BIT BITTER raw in this salad — it needs MACERATION, or just INFUSING THE VINEGAR with the basil instead of leafing it in. Not sure about it yet; stays in want_to_try pending the infusion experiment.

=== WANT TO TRY — GRAPES ===

GRAPES — the other cool-sweet fruit for the pear slot (halved, presumably; the champagne register suits them).
original_chef: Joshua McFadden — Six Seasons (Cucumbers, Scallions, Mint, and Dried Chiles), with my champagne vinegar swap.
